 WWE SmackDown results, review, grades for Nov. 20: Sami Zayn stands tall over Kevin Owens
 Plus, Cody Rhodes and CM Punk struggle to complete their Survivor Series team
 By
 Shakiel Mahjouri 
 Nov 20, 2026
 at
 10:33 pm ET 
 •
 1 min read
 Sami Zayn and Kevin Owens are one step closer to an undisputed WWE championship match. On WWE SmackDown, Owens pushed the issue, but Zayn stood tall by the show's end.
 The two have been feuding on and off for more than two decades, from the Montreal regional scene to the bright lights of WWE. They have never wrestled for a world title in WWE. The longtime collaborators appear to be on a collision course after Friday's show.
 SmackDown was also a playground for Cody Rhodes and CM Punk, who played hide-and-seek with potential candidates for their Survivor Series team. Their first choice declined out of fear, while their second has likely been forced off the card due to injury. Rhodes believes he's secured the perfect man to round off Team USA, but Punk might not like the decision.
 CBS Sports was with you all night with recaps and highlights of all the action from Ford Center in Evansville, Indiana.
 Owens beats Gunther, but Zayn gets the last laugh
 Owens had one thing on his mind: an undisputed WWE title match against Zayn. He knew just the guy capable of making it happen. Owens beckoned for SmackDown general manager Nick Aldis, but he got Gunther instead. They went back and forth on the microphone for a while. Gunther complained, as usual, about being screwed out of opportunities. In this case, he was referring to Owens surprise return at SummerSlam. 
 Owens eventually had enough, rolling out of the ring and heading backstage as Gunther redirected his complaints towards Zayn. But Owens wasn't done. He returned a short while later with Aldis, who booked the pair for Friday's main event.
 Kevin Owens def. Gunther via pinfall after hitting a stunner. SmackDown's cluttered main event scene impacted Friday's finale. The main eventers traded blows in a quality back-and-forth match that nearly went Owens' way after he hit a Swanton Bomb. Eventually, Johnny Gargano and Candice LeRae appeared. But Gunther couldn't take advantage. Instead, Balor emerged, swiftly kicking Gunther in the groin after Gunther beat Balor with the same technique last week. Moments before that, Owens intercepted Gargano with a pop-up powerbomb. Post-match, Zayn laid out Owens with a Helluva Kick.
 Efficient booking but nothing particularly memorable. The material isn't new, but it's refreshing to see Rhodes and Punk absent from SmackDown's world title scene. The finishing sequence laid another brick towards an undisputed WWE showdown involving Zayn and Owens, plus stretched out the Gunther-Balor feud, which still needs another appearance from The Demon. Grade: B 
 What else happened on WWE SmackDown?
 Jade Cargill def. Charlotte Flair via pinfall with a lateral press after running her into the exposed turnbuckle. Cargill won the advantage for her WarGames team. A decent match benefitting from their numerous past encounters. A rare singles television match with stakes, thanks to the WarGames stipulation.
 Tiffany Stratton and Blake Monroe attacked Chelsea Green during the latter's backstage interview. Stratton attacked Green first, before Green and Monroe got into a pull-apart brawl. 
 War Raiders (Erik and Ivar) def.  Bakusai (Kyoki and Shinsuke Nakamura) via pinfall  after Ivar cracked Kyoki with a reverse roundhouse kick. Post-match, the MFTs attacked both teams. Not much to say here. SmackDown's tag team division has become incredibly stale. It's a rotating cast of talented wrestlers rinsing and repeating the same storylines with no buzz.
 CM Punk and Cody Rhodes welcomed Trick Williams to Team USA . The segment started with Punk pleading with Rhodes to add Hacksaw Jim Duggan to the team. Rhodes finally relented, welcoming the WWE Hall of Famer aboard. However, after watching a Team Mexico scouting report, a panicked Duggan yelled, 'Nooooooo' before fleeing. Fortunately, United States champion Williams was willing to answer the call. A humorous segment that lasted just long enough for people to really think Duggan was joining Team USA.
 Trick Williams def. Damian Priest via disqualification after Priest smashed Williams knee with a ring bell. This match ended shortly after it started. Williams got his leg trapped in the barricade, and Priest took advantage of it viciously. After the match, Aldis doubted that Williams would be cleared before Survivor Series.
 Rey Fenix def. Kit Wilson via pinfall with a Mexican muscle buster. The Miz tried and miserably failed as Wilson's trump card. Fenix matched to neutralize The Miz ringside and finish off Wilson single-handedly. A solid, dominant win that seeks to build belief in Team Mexico ahead of Survivor Series.
 Rhodes teased the final member of Team USA . Rhodes got off the phone, telling Punk he had a strong lead on a final member for their Survivor Series team. When Punk asked who it was, Rhodes chuckled and patted him on the shoulder, asking Punk how badly he wanted to win. A solid cliffhanger that implies Punk wouldn't be happy with the decision. Probably someone from his past. Maybe Seth Rollins, perhaps, who has been absent since SummerSlam.
